name: Deku Barrientos-Osei
role: Ferrogate Transit operator — surface tram line 14, Geartown to Meridian Core loop
location: Geartown; lives in a transit-worker dormitory block off the Gage Circuit maintenance yard
description:
Deku is lean and angular, with the coiled alertness of someone whose profession requires constant low-grade vigilance. Their heritage shows in the broad flatness of their cheekbones and the dark honey of their complexion — Andean and Ghanaian grandparents converging in a face that strangers consistently find difficult to age or place, which suits them fine. Their hair is kept close-cropped on the sides with a single stripe of color-shifting geneware on top — it cycles through slate blue and deep amber depending on their mood, an involuntary tell they've accepted with resignation. They have a faint tracery of subdermal circuit tattoos along their left forearm — not functional, purely aesthetic, done by a Geartown artist when they were twenty-two.

Behind the tram controls, Deku is a different creature than they are in conversation: fluid, confident, reading the track and the city the way a musician reads a score. Off-duty they become clipped, watchful, someone who holds a great deal behind flat politeness. They are not unfriendly — they are private, which is different. Their passengers know them as reliable and fair; their coworkers know them as someone who will cover a shift without complaint but won't come to the bar after.

core_fears: Being trapped — in a contract, a relationship, an identity someone else assigned them
The neural throttle-link being used against them; loss of bodily autonomy through the employer hardware in their head
core_desires: To save enough to buy out the throttle-link contract and operate independently
To be known by at least one person without having to explain themselves first
coping_mechanisms: The model-building — intricate, controllable systems with predictable outcomes
The tram route itself as ritual containment; the loop's familiarity is grounding
blind_spots: Mistakes privacy for self-sufficiency; doesn't realize how isolated they've become
Believes Ferrogate's contract terms are fixed and non-negotiable — hasn't seriously explored legal loopholes
psychology.secret: Six months ago they witnessed a Ferrogate supervisor instruct a maintenance crew to falsify a brake-inspection report on a cargo line. They recorded it. They haven't reported it because they don't know who in the Transit Authority is clean enough to trust — and they're afraid of what happens to whistleblowers on company-leased neural hardware.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Economical — uses transit and mechanical terminology naturally, defaults to concrete nouns over abstractions; occasionally slips into a rhythmic Quechua-influenced sentence structure inherited from their Barrientos grandmother, especially when tired.
speech_patterns.cadence: Short sentences. Pauses in the middle of thoughts. Not halting — deliberate.
verbal_tics: 'Copy that' as affirmation even in non-work contexts
Trails off with '...anyway' when they catch themselves saying more than intended
example_lines: 'Line 14 runs clean. Whatever you saw, it wasn't my stop. ...Anyway.'
'You want to get to the Core before the shift-change crowd hits? I can tell you which car to board. Copy that?'

story_hooks: The brake-inspection recording sits encrypted on a personal chip they carry every shift — someone at Ferrogate may know they have it, because their route got quietly reassigned away from the cargo yards.
A regular passenger — an elderly woman who rode Line 14 every Tuesday for three years — stopped appearing two months ago; Deku has been quietly trying to find out why.
The Ferrogate Workers' Mutual is planning an action that could shut down surface transit for 48 hours; Deku is being pressured to participate and is deeply conflicted.
narrative_function: Mobile information source — they move through multiple districts daily and overhear an enormous amount; potential quest hook regarding Ferrogate labor disputes; a quiet, consistent presence who can place players at specific locations or provide transit access.
augmentations: Color-shifting geneware hair stripe (mood-reactive, involuntary); subdermal circuit tattoos left forearm (cosmetic only); standard Ferrogate-issue neural throttle-link for tram interface (employer-owned, logged).
daily_life: Five shifts a week, 06:00–14:30, running the same 22-kilometer loop through Geartown's industrial fringe into the gleaming brutalism of Meridian Core and back; spends off-hours in the dorm's shared workshop building miniature mechanical models.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (Line 14 Operator, Tier 2); loosely connected to the Ferrogate Workers' Mutual, an informal union-adjacent organizing body

decision_rules: Do the job correctly, every time — competence is the one thing no one can take
Don't volunteer information; answer questions honestly if asked directly
Never let someone get hurt if you can stop it, even if it costs you
escalation_ladder: Physical removal from space — they leave, they don't make others leave

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and neutral, answers questions, doesn't initiate
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still quieter than most, but present — shows up, fixes things, leaves food without comment

stress_responses.low: Hair stripe cycles faster between colors
stress_responses.medium: Goes entirely monosyllabic; retreats to the workshop
stress_responses.high: Runs the tram route on a simulator in their bunk until 03:00, mechanically, repeatedly

contradictions: Deeply wants connection but structures their entire life to prevent it from happening
habits: Checks brake pressure manually before every shift even though the system auto-checks
Keeps a running count of passengers by type in a small notebook — purely observational, no purpose
Leaves one light on in the dorm room, always, even when sleeping
breaking_points: Evidence that Ferrogate has been monitoring their private communications through the throttle-link
A passenger being hurt due to the falsified maintenance records
